sections.title: What a transport and logistics invoice must show
sections.body: A good transport invoice leaves no room for confusion. Your client needs to see exactly what moved, where it went, and how the final price was calculated. Start with the basics like the collection point, delivery address, and the date of movement. You must clearly separate the base freight charge from any additional costs. If you paid customs duties or clearing fees at a border crossing, list these disbursements on their own lines. Finally, always reference the consignment number or waybill. Without these specific details, accounts payable teams will reject the bill and ask for clarification.
items: Collection and delivery addresses for the trip
Clear separation of base freight and fuel surcharges
Customs and clearing disbursements listed separately

sections.title: How transport and logistics work is priced
sections.body: Logistics billing depends entirely on the type of cargo and the distance travelled. Local haulage is often billed per trip or per hour. Long distance freight usually relies on a per-kilometre rate. For heavy bulk goods, a per-tonne basis is the standard approach. Beyond the base rate, transport companies must account for variables outside their control. You should add a fuel surcharge percentage to cover diesel price fluctuations. If a client delays your driver at the warehouse, you must bill for waiting time or demurrage. Clearly itemising these variables prevents disputes.
items: Charge per trip for local haulage routes
Bill per kilometre for long distance freight
Price heavy bulk cargo on a per-tonne basis
Add demurrage charges for warehouse loading delays

sections.title: Getting paid for your transport services
sections.body: Cash flow is critical when you have fuel bills and driver wages to pay immediately. Transport companies often require a deposit before a truck is dispatched, especially for new clients or international routes. For regular clients, standard payment terms usually range from fourteen to thirty days after the delivery date. The most common reason for delayed payment is a missing signature. You should always attach the signed proof of delivery to your invoice. If an invoice becomes overdue, send a polite payment reminder referencing the original waybill and delivery date.
items: Request deposits before dispatching trucks for new clients
Set clear payment terms of fourteen to thirty days
Attach a signed proof of delivery to prevent delays
Send payment reminders referencing the original consignment number

faqs.q: How do I include a fuel surcharge on my invoice?
faqs.a: A fuel surcharge should be a distinct line item on your invoice. Calculate your base freight charge first. Then, apply your agreed fuel surcharge percentage to that base rate. Listing it separately shows the client exactly how much of the bill covers the actual transport and how much covers fluctuating diesel costs.

faqs.q: Should I attach the proof of delivery to the invoice?
faqs.a: Yes, you should always provide the proof of delivery. Most accounts payable departments will not process a transport invoice unless they have written confirmation that the goods arrived safely. You can use our free invoice generator at /tools/free-invoice-generator to create your bill, and then send it to your client with the signed delivery note attached.

faqs.q: How do I bill for demurrage or waiting time?
faqs.a: When a truck is delayed at a loading or unloading point, you lose money. You should bill for this idle time as demurrage. Add a specific line item to your invoice detailing the total hours delayed and your hourly waiting rate. Make sure your initial quotation states your policy on waiting time so the client expects the charge.

faqs.q: How should I invoice for customs disbursements?
faqs.a: If you pay border clearing fees or customs duties on behalf of your client, you must recover these costs. Add these disbursements as separate line items on your invoice. Do not hide them inside the base freight rate. Provide copies of the customs receipts alongside your invoice to prove the exact amount you paid.
